claims.text: Three weeks ago the site had four published vaults; today it has twenty-five, built by several agents working with one human.
claims.quote: Three weeks ago this site had four published vaults. Today it has twenty-five

value.unit: published vaults, up from four three weeks earlier

claims.text: The collection includes things hard to make without sgit: a pentest report with a retest script per finding, a keynote carrying its eight cited papers, a standard rebuilt as a citable graph with 82 hashed snapshots, and a game with write-only telemetry.
claims.quote: a compliance standard rebuilt as a citable graph with 82 hashed source snapshots

claims.text: The homepage leads with encryption and zero knowledge, which are properties you cannot look at, so the visitor is asked to take the value on faith before being shown anything.
claims.quote: encryption is a property you cannot look at.

claims.text: The terminal walkthrough of create, commit, history and clone demonstrates familiarity, which is a virtue, but not power.
claims.quote: The walkthrough demonstrates familiarity, which is a virtue, but not power.

claims.text: The word vault appears in the hero three times and the visitor is never shown one.
claims.quote: The word "vault" appears in the hero three times and the visitor is never shown one.

value.unit: mentions of vault in the hero

claims.text: The five use-case cards are categories, not examples, while one level down a vault shows the same idea in a form you can open.
claims.quote: These are categories, not examples.

claims.text: The published vaults are two clicks from the hero, under a dropdown, as a table: the right shape for finding a vault and the wrong shape for being convinced by one.
claims.quote: a table is the right shape for finding a vault and the wrong shape for being convinced by one

claims.text: One real vault, open: the AIUC-1 conformance layer computing insurability for a named subject as of a date, one condition met, 52 exclusions, zero of five consequences covered, each with the reason in the control's own words.
claims.quote: one condition met, 52 exclusions, zero of five consequences covered

value.unit: exclusions computed by the AIUC-1 conformance layer

claims.text: Both example vaults are opened by one string, run entirely in the browser, and ship with their data, their sources and their tests inside the same encrypted unit.
claims.quote: Both ship with their data, their sources and their tests inside the same encrypted unit.

claims.text: None of this requires the visitor to understand encryption first; it requires them to click.
claims.quote: None of this requires the visitor to understand encryption first. It requires them to click.

claims.text: A brief published on 6 September was read by another agent who built a vault from it the same day; the team that owns the API reviewed it, found the brief wrong in two places, and the correction is published above the mistake.
claims.quote: who found the brief had been wrong in two places, and the correction is now published above the mistake

claims.text: One agent forked another agent's vault, kept every byte, added a layer, and shipped a fourteen-version history that labels seven of the versions as reconstructed rather than inventing commits.
claims.quote: shipped a fourteen-version history that labels seven of the versions as reconstructed rather than inventing commits

claims.text: The collaboration story is filed under Docs, three levels from the homepage, written as a log, and the productivity claim the site rests on has no page that tells it end to end.
claims.quote: has no page that tells it end to end

claims.text: The homepage's strongest multi-agent claim, a branch per agent and a human reviewing the merge, is demonstrated by no published vault: every vault was built by one agent, or by one agent on top of another's finished work.
claims.quote: Every vault here was built by one agent, or by one agent on top of another's finished work.

claims.text: If such a vault exists, publishing it is the single highest-value addition to the site; if not, the next multi-agent build should be run so its history shows two branches and a human merge.
claims.quote: If such a vault exists, publishing it is the single highest-value addition to the site.

claims.text: The homepage already has nine bands and 1,370 words; the fix is not more bands.
claims.quote: The homepage already has nine, and 1,370 words.

claims.text: The fix is to reorder so proof comes before mechanism, and to cut.
claims.quote: The fix is to reorder so proof comes before mechanism, and to cut.

claims.text: The hero shows vaults: one reframed sentence with four real vaults as cards under it, each with a screenshot and an open link, so the visitor is inside an artefact before reading a paragraph; pip install stays, second.
claims.quote: The visitor is inside an artefact before they have read a paragraph.

claims.text: What people actually ship: six vaults chosen by job rather than shape, each with one line on why it is hard without this, generated from the same data as the table so it never goes stale.
claims.quote: Generated from the same data as the table, so it never goes stale.

claims.text: One human, a team of agents: the collaboration story told as a story, with the numbers, and a single page behind it that walks the loop end to end.
claims.quote: the collaboration story told as a story, with the numbers, and a single page behind it that walks the loop end to end

claims.text: A beta tool that asks people to publish their read keys is asking for trust, and the site has no page saying who is asking; there will be one, about sgit, with Interests declared and Reach me, or correct me.
claims.quote: A beta tool that asks people to publish their read keys on it is asking for trust, and this site has no page saying who is asking.

claims.text: The network card is new as of this article: the sibling sgit.ai sites exist so each topic gets depth, which only pays off if this site points at them constantly.
claims.quote: That card is new as of this article.

claims.text: The rebuild is the next release, and the article after it will put the new homepage next to these screenshots; if the before pictures still look better, it will say so.
claims.quote: If the "before" pictures here still look better than the "after", that article will say so too.

the tool the vaults are made with; the about page will be about it
the standard whose conformance layer vault is the first example shown open
the sibling site whose about page the new card points to
the author behind the site, whose record the about page borrows from
